title: Guide - Healing and Hope - Honest lament

parts.style: warm, gentle welcome, steady and unhurried
parts.text: Welcome to Healing and Hope. <short pause> This practice is called Honest Lament. <short pause> Here, you don't need careful words, or a brave face. <short pause> You can tell God the truth.

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: Find a position your body can bear for a few minutes. <short pause> Unclench your hands, if they will open. <short pause> If they won't, let them stay as they are. <short pause> Take one breath that doesn't have to be calm. <short pause> It only has to be yours.

Many of us were taught to tidy our prayers before we bring them. <short pause> To say, I'm fine, and I trust You... and nothing in between. <short pause> But the Bible is full of untidy prayers. <short pause> They are called laments. <short pause> A lament is pain that has turned its face toward God. <short pause> It is not a failure of faith. <short pause> It is faith, refusing to stop talking to Him.

David wrote one that is only six verses long. <short pause> Four times in its first two verses, he asks the same question... how long? <short pause> Listen to how it begins, in Psalm thirteen, verse one.
How long wilt thou forget me, O Lord? for ever? how long wilt thou hide thy face from me?

parts.style: slow, reflective, letting the words sink in
parts.text: He says that to God. <short pause> To His face. <short pause> No apology, and no softening. <short pause> And God did not strike those words from the book. <short pause> He kept them... so that you would have them, on a day like this.

So what is your how long? <short pause> How long will this hurt? <short pause> How long until the phone rings, or the body mends, or the house stops feeling so empty? <short pause> Say it to Him now, in your own plain words. <short pause> Begin with... how long, O Lord.

parts.style: slow, deliberate, each phrase landing softly
parts.text: And if there is more, you can say that too. <short pause> Lord, this is what I have lost. <short pause> Lord, this is what I don't understand. <short pause> Lord, this is what I am angry about. <short pause> Lord, this is what I need. <short pause> You don't have to use every line. <short pause> One true sentence is a whole prayer.

Near the end of his psalm, David's questions are still unanswered. <short pause> Nothing around him has changed, that we are told of. <short pause> And yet, beside the questions, he sets down one more true thing. <short pause> It is in verse five.
But I have trusted in thy mercy; my heart shall rejoice in thy salvation.

You may not be ready for that verse today. <short pause> You don't have to hurry to it. <short pause> God can hold your question for as long as it takes. <short pause> And if the pain ever tells you that you would be better off gone, or that you might harm yourself, please don't stay alone with it. <short pause> Call your local emergency number, or a crisis line, or someone who can be with you now. <short pause> That, too, is an honest cry for help.

Let's pray. <short pause> Lord, You heard what I said, and what I couldn't say. <short pause> I have not hidden it from You. <short pause> Do not hide Your face from me. <short pause> Stay in the question with me... <short pause> and when I am able, teach my heart to trust Your mercy again. <short pause> Amen.
You told the truth, and you are still loved. <short pause> There's nothing you need to take back. <short pause> Leave the words with Him... <short pause> and go as softly as you need to.
